title: norite config --json
description:
The machine-readable output of `norite config path | get | set | unset | export | import | split | unsplit` (M21): this machine's client settings, config.toml.

Versioned source of truth (CLAUDE.md rule 15): a change to what these commands print ships with a change to this file in the same commit. The keys themselves are listed in contracts/client-config.toml. Every string here may have come out of a hand-edited file, or out of a file somebody was sent, and is escaped where a terminal would act on it.

`norite config export` with no --output prints the exported TOML document itself, whatever --json says: that output is a config file, not a result.

path.description: The config file these commands mean: config.toml, or one client's own file while the config is split.

split.description: True while `norite config split` has given the terminal client and the GUI a config file each.

client.description: The client whose file `path` is, from --client. Both clients read that file while not split.

key.description: The full key, section.name, as in `tui.colors.accent`.

value.description: The value in force: a string (a color is `"6"` or `"#1e90ff"`), an object for a whole table, or null when nothing sets the key and it has no default.

source.description: `file`: the section asked about sets it. `shared`: a client's section does not, and [shared] does. `default`: nothing in the file sets it. `unset`: nothing sets it and it has no default.

live.description: False for a key whose format is settled and which nothing reads yet.

consumer.description: The milestone that gives the key a reader.

entry.description: One setting as a section sees it. Printed by `get <key>`, `set` and `unset`; the latter two print the key as it is after the change.

warnings.description: What the file holds that was not applied, one sentence each: an unknown key, a value of the wrong kind. At most fifty.

more_warnings.description: How many further warnings were counted and not kept.

entries.description: `norite config get` with no key: every key the contract defines, then any shared key a client's section overrides.

path.description: The file the export was written to.

from.description: What this machine's file set, or null when it did not set the key.

to.description: The value in the imported file.

written.description: True when the file was changed. False for --dry-run and for an import with nothing to change.

applied.description: The keys written, or that would be.

kept.description: Keys both files set differently, left as this machine has them because --overwrite was not passed. `from` is never null here.

skipped.description: What the imported file holds that was not understood, and why.

split.description: The same-machine toggle as it now stands.

files.description: The config files now in use: config.toml when not split, the two clients' own files when split.

base.description: The file an unsplit started from, the more recently saved of the two. Empty for a split.

merged.description: The keys an unsplit added to the base from the other file.

kept.description: The keys both files set differently, where the base's value stayed.

skipped.description: What the other file held that could not be carried over, each with its reason.

backups.description: The files an unsplit set aside, named with .before-unsplit, rather than deleted.

toggled.description: `norite config split` and `norite config unsplit`: what the daemon did. The same shape as daemon-ipc.schema.json's ConfigToggle, which it relays.
